comment: Catalog of OPTIONAL MCP servers and skills for docs/ops/mcp-recommender.cjs. The mandatory minimum (codebase-memory, qmd) is listed apart and is never offered as an extra. Nothing here installs or starts anything. OFFER RULE: the recommender offers only an entry whose provenance is exactly 'host-config' (a concrete version was observed in a client configuration), that is not marked verified:false or unverified, whose pin is concrete and whose install text has no placeholder. Every other entry is never ranked or offered; the recommender lists it under 'not verified, not offered' with the reason. 'author-knowledge' means the entry was written from memory; it stays in the catalog as a record only. An entry whose version could not be taken from a host config or a local lockfile/cache has install null and pin 'unverified: ...'; the operator records a verified version (and provenance host-config) before it may be offered. PIN CONTRACT: an entry is offerable only when pinKind is 'version' and pin is an exact MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH version (optional -prerelease and +build suffix), optionally prefixed by a package name and '@' or '==' (for example @scope/pkg@1.2.3 or pkg==1.2.3), or pinKind is 'revision' and pin is a 40-hex commit (optionally prefixed by 'name@'); and a non-null install is a plain COMMAND that matches the character whitelist [A-Za-z0-9._@/:=+ -] (no quote, | & ; < > ( ) $, backtick, backslash, comma, tab or newline), is split on single spaces into tokens, holds the pin verbatim as exactly one token and holds no other version-like token (digit.digit) and no '-', 'x', 'latest' or 'next' token; prose belongs in the optional 'note' field, which is shown beside the install command and never checked as a command A range (^ ~ * x > < ||), a tag (latest, next), a bare package name, a short or upper-case hash or a branch is never an exact pin. pinKind 'hosted' (a hosted service, not pinnable), 'builtin' (ships with the client) and 'unverified' (no verified version yet) have no exact pin and are never offered; figma, sentry and security-review carry no verified exact pin from a local host config, so they have install null and an unverified pin; the recommender lists them under 'not verified, not offered' with the reason. The loader reports an entry whose install has a non-exact pin in its 'invalid' list and never offers it. cost.tokens is null until somebody measures it with docs/ops/mcp-schema-budget.cjs; a number here would be an invention. network: 'runtime' = the local process calls a remote service while it works; 'none' = no remote call by the server itself (a browser it drives may still open URLs).
